name: ANDE – Paraguay National Hydro
keyPain: Surplus Itaipu allocation exceeding domestic demand; low domestic tariffs limit revenue; monetization pressure from bilateral treaty obligations.
notes: Paraguay law 6.207 provides favorable data-center tariffs. Fast licensing path under 18 months. Political risk: government utility, requires inter-institutional agreements. Competitive advantage: among the cheapest reliable hydro globally.

name: HIVE Digital – ANDE Contracted Block
keyPain: Partial block under-utilized post-BTC mining pivot; seeks AI co-location partner to absorb excess contracted load.
notes: Existing infrastructure: 200 MW substation, fiber, cooling. Can host 3rd-party AI operators within 6 months. Risk: currency/repatriation restrictions in Paraguay.

name: EEP – Ethiopia Hydro (GERD TOU Block)
keyPain: GERD reservoir at capacity; constrained transmission to Addis Ababa; surplus off-peak generation going to waste; international offtake preferred to stabilize project finances.
notes: TOU pricing: off-peak (~3.2¢), peak (~4.5¢). New 500kV corridor under construction to Djibouti (completed 2026 est). Political risk: TPLF region conflict history; improving security. AI/HPC data center special tariff MOUs being offered. Requires USD denominated contracts.

name: Pacifico Energy – Permian BTM Gas
keyPain: EPA flaring regulations tightening in 2026; monetizing associated gas currently flared at Permian Basin wellheads; avoiding regulatory fines.
notes: BTM gas generators avoid ERCOT interconnection queue (direct load). All-in: gas cost + gen O&M ≈ 3.9¢. Sites: Midland, Odessa, Pecos. Can co-locate 10-250 MW modular data center. Timeline: 8-14 months for large deployments. Subject to Railroad Commission permitting.

name: Surge Energy – Permian Stranded Gas
keyPain: High gas-to-oil ratio wells with excess associated gas; flaring cap enforcement looming Q3 2026; seeks long-term industrial gas buyer or captive generation partner.
notes: Lowest cost BTM in region: large gas volumes, low gathering fees. Sites near Crane and Winkler counties. Modular power containers welcome (client-supplied). Willing to sign 5-10 year gas supply agreement with price floor/ceiling.

name: Basin Electric – West ERCOT Substation
keyPain: Excess substation capacity from cancelled industrial project; transmission assets stranded; carrying costs with no load.
notes: Existing 345kV substation near Sweetwater TX. Willing to lease land + substation access. Grid-tied: subject to ERCOT queue but fast-track for existing interconnect upgrades. Best for large hyperscaler seeking ERCOT grid access with infrastructure head start.

name: Confluence Energy – North Dakota Bakken Gas
keyPain: Strict NDIC flaring regulations with production shut-in threats; associated gas volumes exceed pipeline takeaway capacity; seeking captive generation solution immediately.
notes: Potentially lowest cost gas in North America at wellhead (<$0.50/MMBtu). Cold climate advantage: free air cooling for compute (PUE near 1.05). Risk: remote location, fiber access required (~150 mile backhaul). 120 MW expandable to 300 MW with additional wells.

name: Landsvirkjun – Iceland Renewable Grid Block
keyPain: Seeking large stable industrial offtakers for firm capacity; existing aluminum smelter contracts expiring 2027; needs replacement load to maintain project economics.
notes: 100% renewable (geothermal + hydro). Existing heavy-industrial infrastructure. EU regulatory framework; ESG compliance for hyperscalers. Cold climate: free cooling year-round. Fiber: high-latency for some use cases, ideal for training workloads. Timeline: fast, existing interconnect.

name: Rio Grande LNG Adjacent – South Texas Curtailment
keyPain: Frequent wind curtailment in south Texas; generators paid to curtail; seeking industrial load to absorb curtailment and improve project economics.
notes: Flexible pricing: curtailable rate 2-3¢, firm rate 5-6¢. Ideal for Bitcoin mining or AI training workloads that tolerate interruption. 20 miles from LNG terminal (gas backup option). Risk: transmission congestion during high demand.

name: GreenPath – Alberta Stranded Wind
keyPain: New wind capacity exceeding Alberta grid absorption; curtailment averaging 18% of output; needs behind-the-meter or co-located compute load to monetize stranded generation.
notes: Alberta deregulated market. Carbon credit opportunities. USD/CAD FX consideration. Cold climate: PUE advantage. 150-350 MW available with 24-month development. Best for flexible compute (AI training, mining) tolerating ~15% curtailment risk.
